question: The invocation restates Owns, Isolation strategy and Overview for PRD v2 (Success, Constraints), and the citation touch (H13) moves this file's source citations later. How do the restated sentences cite their sources?

options.label: restated text cites PRD v2, the ADRs and the contract guarantees; untouched citations wait for H13
options.consequence: Each rewritten sentence names the PRD v2 section, ADR or contract guarantee it comes from. The Sources field (PRD 1 and Update 1 paths), in the file and in the embedded summary, and the Phase Plan keep their references, so H13's cites-superseded condition still holds and H13 moves them.

options.label: restated text carries no citation
options.consequence: Nothing breaks between steps, but the H18 planner loses the pointer from each Success test and each testing rule to the PRD v2 section, ADR or guarantee that requires it.

options.label: move the Sources field to PRD v2 now
options.consequence: The file reads consistently at once, but the step does H13's work outside the invocation, and H13 would find nothing to move in the header.

chosen: restated text cites PRD v2, the ADRs and the contract guarantees; untouched citations wait for H13
why: Every restated sentence comes from PRD v2 (Success, Constraints, Team and delivery, AC-2.3, AC-4.4, AC-5.5, AC-6.2), ADR-001, ADR-002, auth-api@v1 G3 or booking-api@v1 G5, G10, G17 and Validation, so each says which. S08, S09 and S10 took the same rule for the root, the backend and the web app (DEC-067, DEC-079, DEC-089), so the four specs read alike. The intake record's Sources and Scope paragraph leaves the Sources field to the citation touch.

question: What does simple-login.integration's Owns gain, in its own file and in the embedded summary in hsdd/spec/simple-login.md, for running the real service with its real PostgreSQL beside the real web app and for the scripted tests PRD v2 Success names, given that simple-login.backend's Owns already names the PostgreSQL 17 database, its Docker Compose service and that service's Compose file (S09, DEC-081)?

options.label: the root scripts start PostgreSQL 17 through simple-login.backend's Compose service; the Success tests named; the database stays the backend's
options.consequence: Owns reads: the root package.json scripts, which start PostgreSQL 17 through simple-login.backend's Docker Compose service beside the real service and the real web app; the end-to-end browser test; the scripted tests PRD v2 Success names, each listed; the run instructions. Starting the stack is this node's, the database and its Compose file stay the backend's, so no item has two owners wherever the plan puts the Compose file.

options.label: Owns also claims the Compose file
options.consequence: One file that starts everything sits with the node that runs everything, but it contradicts simple-login.backend's Owns (DEC-081) and PRD v2 Team and delivery, which gives the database to the backend developer: two owners.

options.label: Owns names the Success tests only and leaves the database out
options.consequence: Smaller, but the invocation names Owns for running the real service with its real PostgreSQL, and the H18 planner would not see that the root scripts now start the database (intake record H18: dev and test start PostgreSQL).

chosen: the root scripts start PostgreSQL 17 through simple-login.backend's Compose service; the Success tests named; the database stays the backend's
why: The invocation names Owns for running the real service with its real PostgreSQL beside the real web app, and for the scripted tests PRD v2 Success names. PRD v2 Team and delivery gives the database to the backend developer, and S09 made the database, its Compose service and the Compose file simple-login.backend's wherever the file lives (DEC-081), expecting this node to start it from the root scripts (Q-031). Naming the backend's Compose service in this Owns line keeps that boundary visible from both sides. Does not own was not named by H9 and stays 'any code under backend/ or web/'; this Owns line, not that one, is what keeps a root-level Compose file with one owner. A signal that would have changed this: the intake record giving the Compose file to the integration node.

question: What does simple-login.integration's Isolation strategy say now that the real service keeps bookings in PostgreSQL 17, in its own file and in the embedded summary: the real database only, or also the browser's time zone (routed Q-015, ADR-002) and the real clock?

options.label: real PostgreSQL, never a stand-in; the browser in a zone that is neither account's nor UTC; the real clock
options.consequence: The line reads: none by design: its edges are hard, so it runs the real service on its real PostgreSQL 17, never a mock or an in-memory stand-in (PRD v2 Constraints), beside the real web app, and drives a real browser against them in a time zone that is neither account's nor UTC (ADR-002); the service runs on the real clock. The header states the three conditions every test of this node meets; the plan sets the zone in its Playwright configuration.

options.label: real PostgreSQL only
options.consequence: Strictly what the invocation names, but the browser zone that ADR-002 Consequences require of every browser test would live only in the plan, and the header would not say that nothing here can set the backend's clock, which is why change-day tests and the started cases need their own handling.

chosen: real PostgreSQL, never a stand-in; the browser in a zone that is neither account's nor UTC; the real clock
why: The invocation names the Isolation strategy for running the real service with its real PostgreSQL, and PRD v2 Constraints requires that tests reading or writing bookings use a real PostgreSQL. ADR-002 Consequences require the browser tests to run in an ambient zone that is neither account's nor UTC, and Q-015 routes it to this node; S10 put the same rule in the web app's line (DEC-093) and the orchestrator kept it (DEC-096). Unlike the backend, this node injects no clock: it runs the real service, which is what makes a change-day test take the next change day and a restart stand in for an expired token (ADR-002 Consequences, ADR-001 Consequences). A signal that would have changed this: the intake record keeping test-environment rules out of node headers.

question: How does simple-login.integration's Overview gain the real PostgreSQL and the scripted tests PRD v2 Success names, given that it says the node 'drives a browser through every acceptance criterion in the PRD', and how much of the testing design does it state?

options.label: restate it: the stack with the database, the three Success tests with their guarantees, and what running on the real clock means
options.consequence: Paragraph 1 keeps the node's role and the one command, now starting PostgreSQL 17 with the service and the web app, and says the database and its Compose service are simple-login.backend's. A short list names the three Success tests with the guarantees they check (booking-api@v1 G5; AC-4.4; booking-api@v1 G17 with auth-api@v1 G3, so the restart test signs in again). A last paragraph states the consequences of the real clock: the next change day after it, never a fixed date (ADR-002, booking-api@v1 G10); a restart as AC-2.3's expired-token stand-in (auth-api@v1 G3); the started cases left to the plan; the proxy replay limited to fixtures the running service can answer. The 3-second check of PRD 1 is not named.

options.label: append one sentence naming the Success tests
options.consequence: Smallest change, but the H18 planner would not read here why a restart test must sign in again, why a change-day test cannot use a fixed date, or that some booking-api fixtures cannot be replayed through the proxy, all of which follow from this node running the real service on the real clock.

options.label: state the test mechanics too (HTTP or browser for the 20 attempts, the third zone's name, a database per test run)
options.consequence: A fuller Overview, but it takes decisions that belong to the H18 plan and would leave the plan with an Overview to contradict.

chosen: restate it: the stack with the database, the three Success tests with their guarantees, and what running on the real clock means
why: The invocation names the Overview for running the real service with its real PostgreSQL beside the real web app and for the three Success tests. Each added sentence restates a PRD v2 section, an ADR consequence or a contract guarantee (booking-api@v1 G5, G10, G17, Validation; auth-api@v1 G3; ADR-001 and ADR-002 Consequences), so the Overview adds no rule of its own; the mechanisms stay with the H18 plan, to which the routed items are carried. Q-025 asks that this touch not name PRD 1's 'Home within 3 seconds' as a PRD criterion; the new Overview names PRD v2 Success only, and whether a new phase keeps the shipped assertion stays with the plan.

question: PRD v2 Success asks that every acceptance criterion pass in a scripted test, and H9 puts that test in this node. The backend's clock decides whether a booking has started (ADR-002 Decision 5), and this node runs the service on the real clock. Does the Overview say this node proves every criterion end to end, including a booking that has started (AC-5.5, AC-6.2), or that the plan names the scripted test covering those?

options.label: the plan names the scripted test that covers a criterion turning on the backend's clock
options.consequence: The Overview says every acceptance criterion passes and, for a booking that has started (AC-5.5, AC-6.2), leaves to the H18 plan which scripted test covers it. Asking for a started time works under the real clock, but a booking of one's own that has started appears only by waiting for its start or by writing to the backend's database, so the plan weighs a slow end-to-end test against citing the backend's injected-clock test.

options.label: this node proves every criterion end to end
options.consequence: One place holds the whole Success criterion, but it commits the plan to waiting up to a quarter hour of real time in the suite or to writing bookings into a database simple-login.backend owns, before the planner has weighed either.

chosen: the plan names the scripted test that covers a criterion turning on the backend's clock
why: Q-015 (from S04) routes exactly this to the integration plan: the backend's clock decides started, an end-to-end test cannot set it, so the plan says which scripted test covers AC-5.5 and AC-6.2's started case. PRD v2 Success requires a scripted test, not a browser test, and booking-api@v1 Validation already makes sequence properties the producer's own tests and this node's. A spec-level statement that this node proves both end to end would pre-empt that plan decision. A signal that would have changed this: PRD v2 asking for every criterion in a browser.

question: Q-008, Q-015, Q-020, Q-021, Q-024 and Q-025 target H18, simple-login.integration's phase-plan-append, and reached this spec touch only because H18's target is the same node; the step must close every routed item, and a closed item no longer reaches H18. How are they closed?

options.label: close each as explained and carry its text to H18
options.consequence: Each is closed 'explained', naming what of it the touched header and Overview now state, and the report routes one consider item per original to H18 with the original text, prefixed by where it came from. H13, the citation touch on the same node, will match the carried items in turn and face the same choice.

options.label: close each as addressed
options.consequence: True only for the clauses the header and Overview now state (the restart signing in again, the restart as AC-2.3's stand-in, the third browser zone, the next change day, the started cases left to the plan, the replay limited to answerable fixtures, no 3-second criterion); the rest (Asia/Kolkata, the 2027-03-28 date, the strings to assert, the fourteen replayable fixtures, profileFixture's timeZone, keeping or dropping the 3-second assertion) would vanish from H18.

options.label: leave them open
options.consequence: Keeps them for H18 untouched, but the step's done-when requires every routed item in closes.

chosen: close each as explained and carry its text to H18
why: S09 and S10 met the same mechanics for H14 and H16 and chose this (DEC-085, DEC-095); the orchestrator kept it (DEC-087, DEC-097). All six items are plan content for H18 that a spec touch may not write into the Phase Plan; their spec-level clauses are now in the header and Overview (DEC-100 to DEC-102), and the rest must still reach the planner.
evidence: hsdd/auto/queue.jsonl (Q-027 to Q-030, Q-034 to Q-036)

question: S11's report lists reads outside its inputs (the root scripts, the Playwright config, e2e tests, verification docs, earlier step records) and carried six items to H18 as S09 and S10 did. Keep the output or rework?

options.label: Keep the output
options.consequence: The integration node's text stands; the six carried items reach H18 with their text and kind.

options.label: Rework
options.consequence: No different result: the reads grounded the shipped rig's facts (no database started, the restart stand-in), and the carrying follows from B-10 (DEC-087).

why: All reads are inside the repository; none is out of bounds. Reading the shipped rig is how the step saw that it starts no database and that bookings would persist across test runs, both routed to H18. A read outside the repository would have changed this.
